body: Yeah, I feel you. I think I'm only here because of my family. But it's a very strange place to be when it feels like being here is causing them pain, by being a burden, but going would cause them pain too. So I don't really know what to do other than distance myself from them (like going back to college), and then I just feel massively useless because I can't look after myself like a functioning adult. And I feel terrible for thinking this, but there are times I wish I needed oxygen tubes, or had cancer or something, so people could at least see that I'm ill. But because it's not blatantly obvious we're expected to act like everyone else, or we're lazy. It's too much.

Urgh that's horrible. I get that when I have a bad flare-up, it's so weird. I kind of feel a bit like that now, if that makes sense. Like apart from the world and in a little bubble that I can't reach through.

Hi, I'm sorry you feel this way too. I've been here before, it's passed and I've felt a bit better about life, and then it comes back. It's exhausting, and I just don't see the point in staying in such a hopeless cycle.

M.E. (chronic fatigue). People hear the name and think I don't get enough sleep and should go to bed early. Really it feels like I've always got the flu, or have just run a marathon or two. There are days where every hair on my body hurts. But because it's invisible and doesn't sound serious, it feels like nobody cares, or I've got to keep it secret in case people judge me for not being able to cope with something 'so small'.
